description_en: Mati Bāhācā is a small courtyard containing two small monuments: one is a small shrine with Buddha’s image, and the other is apañcāvaliyukta caitya. There is another courtyard is on the route leading from Naka Bahī to Dhalāyacā; one can cross through this to reach the Mati Bāhācā courtyard. This courtyard is not in fact abahāḥ.Rather, it derives its name from Mati Bahā, and the fact that it is small in size. In 1863 CE (NS 983), Govinda Siṃha and his wife Vidyā Lakṣmī established apañcāvaliyukta caityainside the courtyard in memory of their son Jitamāna. After this, the courtyard began to be known as Govindasiṃha Vihāra. Local inhabitants also call this place Cibhāḥ Cuka.Apancāvaliyukta caityatypically has five layers, consisting of images of lotuses, water, jewels,vajraand fire, and this one does not deviate from this structure. On the top of these layers (āvalis) is the sanctum (garbha) of the Caitya. Below thisgarbhaone can find images of Buddha at each of the four cardinal directions. Five small images of Lakhinarasiṃha, Jitamāna, Matiju, Govindasiṃha and Vidyā Thakuṃ have been engraved on the Caitya’s western plinth. There is an oil-lamp balustrade surrounding the Caitya, which spans over the RCC beams. These in turn are supported by short pillars.To the south of the Caitya is a small shrine made of stone with an image of Akṣobhya Buddha in its niche facing north. This shrine has been constructed on a plinth measuring 70 cm high and with a solid brick core. The Buddha image is housed in a smaller arched niche, also made of brick, which is covered by the stone slab roof of the stone temple. The stone temple structure itself measures 35 cm x 80 cm. The overall size of the temple is 150 cm x 120 cm, and it is 220 cm high. Its two-layered stone roof is decorated with lotus petals and crowned by a singleãvaḥsāḥstonegajū.This in turn is backed by a brick masonry wall with a width equal to that of the stone temple. To the north of this shrine is apañcāvali caityaconstructed on a plinth measuring 150 cm high on a square base of 116 cm. There is also a newly established shrine for Sarasvatī near this shrine.This courtyard is accessible from Mati Bāhā (to the west) through a narrow opening demarcated by two carved columns that are 120 cm in height. This route is open duringmatayāḥand other such festivals.
description_ne: मति बाहाचा बुद्धको प्रतिमा भएको एउटा देवल र एउटा पञ्चापवलियुक्त चैत्य भएको एउटा सानो चोक हो । नक बहीबाट धलायचा जाने बाटोमा एउटा चोक छ, त्यो चोक पार गरेपछि मति बाहाचा चोकमा पुगिन्छ । यो चोक मति बाहाको नजिकै रहेको छ र यो आकारमा सानो छ, त्यसैले यसलाई मति बाहाचा भनिएको हो । वास्तवमा यो कुनै बाहा होइन, एउटा चोक मात्र हो । नेसं ९८३ (सन् १८६३) मा गोविन्दसिंहले पत्नी विद्यालक्ष्मीसहित भएर छोरा जितमानको स्मृतिमा चोकभित्र एउटा पञ्चापवलियुक्त चैत्य स्थापना गरे, पछि त्यही चोकलाई गोविन्दसिंह विहार भन्न थालियो । स्थानीय वासिन्दाहरू यसलाई चिभा चुक पनि भन्दछन् ।पञ्चापवलियुक्त चैत्यमा पद्म, जल, मणि, वज्र र अग्निका पाँच आवलि वा तह हुन्छन् । ती तहभन्दा माथि चैत्यको गर्भ बनाइएको हुन्छ । गर्भभन्दा मुनि यस चैत्यमा चारै दिशामा बुद्धका प्रतिमा छन् । चैत्यको पश्चिमी पेटीमा लक्ष्मीनरसिंह, जितमान, मतिजु, गोविन्दसिंह र विद्या थकुंका स-साना प्रतिमा कुँदिएका छन् । चैत्यको रिङ्गै दीपमालिका बनाइएको छ जुन छोटा पिल्लरद्वारा अड्याइएका आरसिसि बिममाथि जडिएको छ ।चैत्यको दक्षिणपट्टि अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको पश्चिमाभिमुख प्रतिमा रहेको सानो देवल रहेको छ । त्यो देवलको नजिकै केही समय अगाडि बनेको सरस्वतीको स्थान रहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Govinda Siṃha and his wife Vidyā Lakṣmī established thispañcāvaliyukta caityain memory of their son Jitamāna.
This shrine was constructed in memory of Govinda Siṃha and Vidyā Thakũ by their grandson Harṣarāja and his wife Harṣa Thakũ.
